source_quality.equation_authority: text layer plus cropped renders of the equation pages

task_reconstruction.official_task: 2025 MCM Problem C, Olympic medal counts, with a coaching question and a policy question.
required_outputs: a 2028 medal forecast with intervals and a comparison with 2024
the probability that a country wins its first medal
the effect of the event program and of the host
a quantified great-coach contribution for three countries

section_map.summary: summary: the fused frame, three probabilities, three countries for coaches
introduction: the tie, the three tasks, the review that refuses the trees
assumptions: no postponement, no politics, no statistical error
data: named merges, a right skew, a host sample of one percent
model: Poisson and the zero-inflated model refused, then the hurdle
validation: coverage, and the tobit win that costs the non-zero medals
host: two mechanisms, and a dual strategy
coach: the smoothed score and the detected years
insights: the host effect fades by about twenty percent
sensitivity and evaluation: a bound of ten percent, and one weakness

contributions.summary: The models are kept only after Poisson and the zero-inflated model are refused in turn.
The hurdle multiplies a logit probability by a truncated expectation.
The coach enters the medal equation only through its fitted value.
The host effect is read at two horizons and said to fall by about twenty percent.

dependency_graph.label: The advantage index enters the latent index.
The same index feeds both stages of the hurdle.
The smoothed score is the instrument.
The detected years mark the coach.

assumptions.summary: The Games are held on schedule, so a postponement will not occur.
Politics and bans are shut out, and the model uses only the existing data.
The data are declared real and without statistical errors.
The score is correlated with the coach and does not enter the medal count directly.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Country names, athlete names, and event names are harmonized, and the printed cases are kept.
The host is one percent of the observations, and the paper repeats its caution.
The athlete count is cut into four bins because the future count is unknown.
The medal colors are smoothed because a one-two-three coding creates false changes.

models.summary: MU-C-Q255-001: the advantage index, with both readings.
MU-C-Q255-002: the latent index and the truncation at zero.
MU-C-Q255-003: the logit and the truncated count, multiplied.
MU-C-Q255-004: the coach indicator fit in two stages.
MU-C-Q255-005: the weighted total and the fading window.
MU-C-Q255-006: the change detector, with no posterior printed.

verification.summary: Hurdle coverage 88.6 percent against tobit coverage 83.8 percent, on 192 countries.
Tobit is exact on 69.1 percent of the zero-medal countries, hurdle on 41.3 percent.
United States volleyball changes in 2008 at posterior 0.95, gymnastics in 1984 at 0.87.
Three replacement classifiers move the coefficients by less than 10 percent.

results_trace.summary: The largest rises are the United States 15, China 10, India 7, Brazil 5, and Japan 5.
The declines are France, Russia, Germany, Great Britain, and Australia.
Angola 49.23 percent, Bangladesh 46.67 percent, Cambodia 42.49 percent.
The United States is given rowing and triathlon at 2, and the other two countries at 1.
The host coefficient falls from 1.354 to 1.085, read as about 20 percent.

writing_logic.summary: Each model gets its job before the shared inputs are named.
Two candidates are refused, each for a named assumption, before the hurdle is defined.
The tobit win is kept and then priced.
Three estimators are named in the sentence that abandons them.
The weakness blames the subject and names the missing factors.

The box plots of total medals from 1896 to 2024, read as a right skew.
The correlation among the medal counts, read as collinearity.
The heatmap of the advantage index by country and sport.
The four forecasts against the 2024 counts.
The 2028 gold, silver, and bronze by country.
The advantage index, the events, and the total for four countries.
The sports that contribute most for the United States and for Egypt.

The two kinds of change the detector is meant to find.
The medal series before and after the smoothing.
The two-stage fit and the plain fit against the medals.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The summary prints 42.5 percent for Cambodia, and the table prints 42.49 percent.
The prose says Hurdle and Hurdle perform better, naming one model twice.

weaknesses.summary: The closing line of the review prints Herdle for Hurdle.
The Poisson citation prints Blais-Morissetr, and the section title prints Ramdom Forest.
The comparison sentence prints Hurdle and Hurdle.
The strength prints Topit, and the insight heading prints Double-Eged.
The cleaning prints Tabble Tennis, and the host caution repeats its own clause.
The first-stage slope is printed with a partial derivative sign.

independent_extensions.summary: Report a first-stage strength for the coach instrument, which the paper does not.
Give numerical values to the medal weights a, b, and c, which the display leaves symbolic.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Define the chosen model against the one just refused.
Price a win by the ability it costs.

unresolved_questions: What numerical weights sit on gold, silver, and bronze inside the smoothed score?
How strong is the first stage of the coach regression?
Which of the two printed Cambodia probabilities, 42.5 or 42.49, is the computed one?
